name: Princeps Nashville Staging Host

securitySheaf.label: Visitor Badge Challenge
securitySheaf.effect: The procurement front desk runs your vendor credential against the day's approved buyer list and holds the lobby until a human verifier signs off.

securitySheaf.label: Threat Correlation
securitySheaf.effect: Your signature is correlated against archived attack traffic on Cross Applied Technology, and your visitor file is reclassified as suspect.

securitySheaf.label: Tasking Fork
securitySheaf.effect: Your session's tasking metadata is forked into plant dossiers, and every requisition you file inherits a flagged-buyer routing code.

securitySheaf.label: Handler Approval Loop
securitySheaf.effect: Each action you take is filed as a requisition awaiting a handler countersignature that never clears, pinning you to the counter.

securitySheaf.label: Tasking Vault Custody
securitySheaf.effect: The vault custodian treats the session as hostile penetration of compartmented tasking and seals the compartment with you inside it.

sculpting: From the outside a bland CAS procurement office of requisition counters and vendor portals, but behind the filing wall sit compartmented ops rooms staging strikes on Cross Applied Technology.
notes: Staging host for the Cross Applied Technology arc: deckers breach the procurement front to trace tasking, and the sheaf escalates from badge checks to terminal black IC guarding the vault. Attribution evidence is a lead, not proof against any named Princeps principal.

nodes.title: Procurement Vestibule
nodes.description: An immaculate front vestibule where every door asks for a stated reason. Notices are current, directories are neat, and nothing here admits it hides anything.

nodes.title: Public Tender Board
nodes.description: Official requisition notices and liaison directories, posted for any registered vendor. Everything is legible, ordinary, and completely unremarkable.

nodes.title: Vendor Records Room
nodes.description: Routine vendor records filed exactly as expected, except one folder sits out of place, uncatalogued and slightly warm to the touch.

choices.label: Look for the Deep Archive seam

nodes.title: Odd Requisition Memo
nodes.description: A Princeps Huntsville letterhead memo names a "Lafayette package" with a delivery window, and nothing more. Tell the GM exactly what you found and ask them to confirm scope.

report.title: Lafayette package requisition memo
report.detail: Mevin recovered a Princeps Huntsville letterhead requisition naming a "Lafayette package" with a delivery window. Confirm the memo's date, author field, and whether the delivery window matches a known incident before the crew acts on it.

nodes.title: Device Ledger
nodes.description: Procurement entries for field devices whose delivery windows match a known dead drop. Timing lines up neatly; names and orders do not appear anywhere.

report.title: Field device procurement ledger
report.detail: Mevin copied device procurement entries whose delivery windows align with a known utility dead drop. Ask the GM which entries are corroborated and whether the ledger itself is a plant.

nodes.title: Unindexed Seam
nodes.description: A route that should not be indexed, stitched between filing routines and missed by every audit pass. The system forgets it exists whenever you look away.

choices.label: Back out to the vendor files

nodes.title: Guardhouse Slave Panel
nodes.description: Apparent access to the leased site's cameras and door badge reader. Tell the GM what you see and ask what the site actually covers before you trust it.

report.title: Leased-site camera and badge access
report.detail: Mevin reached the leased site's camera and door-badge slave systems. Confirm which cameras exist, whether badge history is readable, and what the physical site actually covers.

nodes.title: Deep Archive
nodes.description: Compartmented ops records behind numbered doors and sealed dispatch boxes. The order here is military discipline, not menace, and every section keeps its own counsel.

choices.label: Copy the Lafayette package tasking file

nodes.title: Attribution Cache
nodes.description: A recovered package of tasking, procurement, and payment records tying the staging to Princeps as a lead. Worth nothing unless you walk out carrying it.

report.title: Attribution cache recovered
report.detail: Mevin reached a package of tasking, procurement, and payment records implicating Princeps as a lead only. The GM decides whether any document is authentic, altered, a plant, or a deliberate signature, and whether Claude August or any named principal is actually tied to the attacks.

nodes.title: False-Flag Plant
nodes.description: You seed the compartment with a dispatch blaming someone else for the staging. The audit trail records the tampering the moment you do it. Notify the GM before you commit.

report.title: False-flag dispatch planted
report.detail: Mevin planted a fabricated dispatch inside the ops compartment. The GM must decide who benefits, whether the tamper-evident seal flags Princeps's own audit log, and how Princeps reacts once the plant is discovered.

nodes.title: Clean Exit
nodes.description: The cover surface closes back over the intrusion. Notices refresh, directories settle, and the vestibule is once again the most boring place on the grid.
